core_obligations: Pass to adjoints (proof lines 8444-8445): going around either side of the displayed diagram yields the map adjoint to a map Lf^*(Rf_*K tensor^L Rf_*L tensor^L Rf_*M) -> K tensor^L L tensor^L M.
Compute the source (proof lines 8446-8451): use monoidality of Lf^* to rewrite the source as Lf^*(Rf_*K) tensor^L Lf^*(Rf_*L) tensor^L Lf^*(Rf_*M).

Identify the two composites (proof lines 8452-8456): each side of the diagram gives, after transposition, the same map obtained from the canonical maps Lf^*Rf_* -> id, so the two composites agree and the diagram commutes in D(O').
proof_roadmap: Transpose both composites along the Lf^* - Rf_* adjunction.
Rewrite the transposed source using monoidality of the derived pullback.
Observe that both sides give the same map to K tensor^L L tensor^L M.
Conclude commutativity of the diagram in D(O').
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the relative cup product is associative, i.e. that the two bracketing composites of the displayed diagram agree in D(O') (statement lines 8421-8441). The proof does not compare the composites directly: it transposes them along the derived adjunction and computes the transposed source using monoidality of the derived pullback, Lf^*(Rf_*K tensor^L Rf_*L tensor^L Rf_*M) = Lf^*Rf_*K tensor^L Lf^*Rf_*L tensor^L Lf^*Rf_*M (proof lines 8444-8451), so that both sides are recognised as the same adjoint map into K tensor^L L tensor^L M. The non-formal move is this transposition and the resulting identification of two apparently different composites. The claim is H2: one adjunction computation, written out in a single display.
